# ZeroBlur Alternative: Which Screen Blur Extension Should You Use?

Blur sensitive data on your screen in one click.

100% local — no cloud, no sign-up. Works in live demos, calls, and screen recordings.

ZeroBlur and DataBlur compared side by side

DataBlur is the closest ZeroBlur alternative: both blur sensitive data on screen before a screen share or recording, but DataBlur adds automatic detection of emails, credit cards and API keys, redact and transparent hide styles, and a fail-safe that blurs more — not less — when something goes wrong. ZeroBlur is still a fine pick if all you need is to hand-blur a few elements, free with no strings attached. [...] ### Is DataBlur a free ZeroBlur alternative?

Yes. Manual blur, area blur, auto-detection, redact and transparent styles, the blur list and keyboard shortcuts are all free, with no signup. The free version marks auto-applied blurs with a small badge; DataBlur Pro removes it and adds saved profiles.

### Does either extension send my data to the cloud?

DataBlur processes everything locally — no cloud, no AI, no data ever leaves your device, which is why it can be used in front of client data. ZeroBlur does not document a cloud component either; check its site for the current details.

### Can I blur data automatically instead of clicking each field? [...] With DataBlur, yes: auto-detection finds emails, card numbers, passwords and API keys on its own, and the blur list hides every match of your own keywords or regex patterns. ZeroBlur is manual by design — you select each element or area yourself.

## Hide it before it leaks

Both tools beat editing blur boxes into a recording afterwards. If your screen only occasionally holds something sensitive, ZeroBlur is a perfectly good, perfectly free answer. If your screen holds client data every day, let the tool do the hunting: install DataBlur free and see what auto-detect catches on your own dashboard.

Keep your blurs. Drop the watermark.

Blurring is always free. Pro lets you save blur profiles and removes the watermark. One product, your choice of plan.

results.title: ContextBlur vs Datablur: Feature-by-Feature Comparison (2026)
results.content:
For most users, ContextBlur's free tier provides enough functionality for daily use. The Pro upgrade is a modest investment for those who need full auto-detection and unlimited blurs. Check out our full tools comparison for more options.

## When to Choose ContextBlur

ContextBlur is the right choice if you:

 Need automatic PII detection to catch what you might miss manually
 Want blur rules that persist across page loads and browser sessions
 Work in a field that requires zero data collection for compliance
 Prefer a polished side panel interface for mid-session adjustments
 Value an open-source, auditable codebase
 Want to explore BlurWeb comparisons and other alternatives

## When to Choose Datablur

Datablur may suit you better if you: [...] Toggle Selection Mode on/off
 Run auto-blur with configurable detection types
 View the count of currently blurred elements
 Clear all blurs with one click

Datablur takes a simpler approach with a popup interface and hotkey support. It is straightforward to use, but lacks the persistent side panel that makes ContextBlur easy to control during live screen sharing sessions without switching windows.

For professionals who need to adjust blurs mid-presentation, having the side panel open alongside your content is a meaningful workflow advantage.

## User Base and Community [...] ContextBlur saves your blur selections per URL using CSS selectors stored in your browser's local storage. When you revisit a page -- whether it is your CRM dashboard, an HR portal, or a client's project board -- your blurs are automatically restored. You configure once and forget about it. This is especially valuable for pages you visit daily during recurring meetings or presentations.

Datablur does not persist blurs between sessions. Every time you reload a page or navigate away and back, you need to re-apply your blurs from scratch. For a one-time screen share, this is fine. For recurring workflows, it means repeated manual effort before every meeting.

If you need to blur image-based or canvas content: BlurWeb or Page Blur. The rectangle-draw tool handles content that element-level blurring cannot.

If you want free with zero complexity: ZeroBlur. No features, no cost, no learning curve.

If you want a one-time purchase: BlurWeb's lifetime deal on AppSumo is the established option in this space.

For most remote work teams, ContextBlur gives the best operational tradeoff: less repetitive setup, fewer missed fields, and a cleaner pre-call routine. That matters more in practice than feature-count comparisons.

## A Note on Trust and Privacy

When you install a screen blur extension, you are giving it access to the content of every webpage you visit. That is a significant trust grant. Before installing any extension, check: [...] ## TL;DR — Best Screen Blur Extension in 2026

If you want one recommendation and no spreadsheet: choose ContextBlur for most recurring workflows. Choose BlurWeb when area-draw blur is non-negotiable. Choose ZeroBlur if your only requirement is “free and simple.”

> Verdict at a glance
>
>  Best overall for recurring business demos: ContextBlur
>  Best for area blur + Firefox workflows: BlurWeb
>  Best fully free fallback: ZeroBlur
>  Best for occasional manual blur with flexibility: Datablur / Page Blur

## The Screen Blur Extension Landscape in 2026 [...] 1. ContextBlur -- Element-level blurring with auto-blur rules and sensitive data detection
2. BlurWeb -- Click-to-blur and rectangle-draw blurring with AppSumo lifetime deal
3. Datablur -- Screen blur with multiple blur methods and hotkey support
4. ZeroBlur -- Lightweight free blur extension
5. Page Blur -- Simple blur with area selection

Other extensions exist (Blur It, Privacy Screen, BlurScreen), but these five represent the range of approaches and price points in the category.
